item: A custody entry owed for a reused article id is written, not settled by the previous article's entry
summary: pending.drain settled an owed entry as already present when ANY INGEST entry existed for article:<id>. articles.id has no AUTOINCREMENT, so a deletion, or a restore's swap discarding the articles committed after its working copy, hands the same ids out again, while the append-only custody log keeps the earlier article's entry; a new article that took the id and whose own custody write failed was never given its entry and nothing said so. drain now settles an entry only when an INGEST entry at the id carries the article's own content hash (the record's, else the stored row's); another hash leaves the entry to be written, marked earlier_ingest_other_hash; when the hash cannot be learned yet the entry stays queued. Failing test first: 3 of 6 tests red on the previous pending.py. gap_scan is unchanged and stays id-only (Article.hash is rewritten in place by other lanes, so a hash compare there would report false gaps). Not observed in the field: the mechanism is read from the code and driven by the tests.
